claims.statement: Lemma thm:surplus / eq:unified-identity hold for every policy of every regime (R1 ex-ante, R2 cascades incl. noisy verifiers and v_c, R3 chain trace and its variants, constants, oracle bound) on id_test, OOD176 and RouterBench, in dollars and (id_test) seconds; the four terms of eq:cascade-surplus sum to Q and S
claims.result: 486 policies x 1001 bootstrap rows: max |residual|/|eta| = 2.1e-14 (dollars), 1.9e-15 (seconds, 266 id_test policies); max decomposition residual 5.6e-14
claims.note: Code check: the identity is algebra on paired outcomes (Y_B, C_B observed for every task); the R3 chain uses H = 1{Opus not run}, A = sum of cheap attempt costs.

claims.statement: Ranking of the regimes by eta/eta_B (best policy per regime, paired 95% CIs): id_test (R3 = counterfactual ACRouter map + oracle cascade), OOD176 (R3 = released trace), RouterBench (R1 = our LR router, R3 = LR + oracle cascade)
claims.result: id_test: R1(6.32) > R2(2.00) > R3-cf(1.39); OOD176: R1(24.29) > R1-mem(13.25) > R3(2.59) > R2(1.91); RouterBench: R1(20.58) > R2(2.89) > R3-cf(1.39) (adjacent gaps CI-decided: id_test True, OOD176 True, RouterBench True). Under the quality floor eps <= 0.01: id_test R1(6.32) > R2(2.00) > R3-cf(1.39); OOD176 R3(2.59) > R2(1.91); RouterBench R2(2.89) > R3-cf(1.39) > R1(1.08)
claims.note: Descriptive: the best policy of each regime is selected on the same sample it is evaluated on (in-sample selection); RouterBench R1 decisions come from a router fitted on the disjoint 70% split.

claims.statement: Where the in-loop verification of the R3-OOD trace pays: four-term decomposition of its net gain against always-Opus and the same terms for its chain variants (single primary + oracle -> Opus; longer chains; unconditional / gated / no escalation)
claims.result: R3 trace: eta/eta_B 2.59 [1.97, 3.54], E[V] 0.733 [0.670, 0.795] vs Opus 0.636, E[D] $0.493 vs $1.107; net gain 0.783 [0.549, 1.057] $/task = avoided reference work 0.876 - attempt cost 0.262 + accepted quality change/eta_B +0.168 - recovery 0.000; e = 0.051. Variants: MiniMax + oracle -> Opus (R2) 1.41 [1.25, 1.65]; chain[4] always escalate 1.66 [1.41, 2.11] (E[V] 0.784); chain[4] never escalate 4.72 [3.79, 5.97] (E[V] 0.710). Gate 'applied_in_cheap >= 2' as a signal for Opus success among chain-failed tasks: P(Opus resolves | escalated) = 0.14 vs P(Opus resolves | not escalated) = 0.41; TPR 0.31, FPR 0.66. 168/469 attempts are unrecorded runs billed at $0 (imputed-cost sensitivity: eta/eta_B 1.75)
claims.note: Descriptive. The trace is a deterministic replay of the outcome matrix (verified 176/176), so its verifier is the ground-truth test outcome (TPR = 1, FPR = 0 by construction) and erroneous acceptance comes only from the give-up branch (chain exhausted, no escalation).

claims.statement: R1 lookup/ex-ante routers versus R2 oracle cascades under the quality floor E[V] >= vbar - eps: which policies satisfy eps <= 0.01, and how the efficiency ranking changes under the floor
claims.result: id_test: R1 10/10 satisfy eps=0.01 (eps=0.05: 10), R2 14/14 (theta=1: Q >= 0 for all: True); OOD176: R1 0/5, R2 7/7, R3 trace 1; RouterBench: R1 1/5, R2 20/20. Floor-feasible bests (eta/eta_B): id_test R1: routellm_mf (6.32), R2: Qwen3-Max θ=0.5 (2.00), R3-cf: ACRouter map + oracle θ=0.5 -> Opus (1.39); OOD176 R2: gpt-5.4 + oracle (1.91), R3: ACRouter chain (k=2) (2.59); RouterBench R1: LR (lambda=0η_B) (1.08), R2: gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 θ=0.5 (2.89), R3-cf: LR (lambda=1η_B) + oracle theta=1 (1.39)
claims.note: In-sample classification with CI-decided flags per policy (see the floor table). At theta = 1 an oracle hit has Y_P = 1 >= Y_B, so Q >= 0 is automatic for R2; R1 routers trade quality for cost and can violate the floor while winning on eta.

claims.statement: X7 live parts: R2 with real verifiers (LLM judge, sandbox in-prompt tests) and R3 on id_test (ACRouter release mode + escalation variant), and the operating-point prediction of the R3 - R2 sign from measured (kappa_ver, TPR, FPR, cbar_h)
claims.result: Not measurable offline: ACRouter ID mode dispatches once per task (no within-task escalation in the released id_decisions.jsonl), the released routers ship no verifier scores, and the only R3 trace (OOD176) uses the ground-truth test outcome as its verifier
claims.note: Pending X7-b (collection A/B). The offline counterfactual "ACRouter map + oracle verify-then-escalate" is reported as what the live id_test variant would reach with a perfect, free verifier (the verifier-side bound: e = 0 at theta = 1, no verification cost); it is not an efficiency bound, see deviation 1 and the per-decision optimal-escalation bound.
